16.1.title: Can it deploy — fresh clone viability
evidence: README.md:163-170 documents clone → npm install → npm run dev -- --turbopack
README.md:182 says 'Copy .env.example to .env and fill in your keys. The demo mode works without credentials.'
src/app/api/analyze/route.ts:13 checks `process.env.DEMO_MODE === 'true' || cacheExists()` — demo mode fallback works without API keys
src/data/cache/ contains 9 pre-generated JSON files (wallet-a-ethereum.json, personas.json, roast-battle.json, etc.) — checked into the repo, not gitignored
src/lib/cache.ts:10 references 'Run scripts/seed-demo.ts first' but no such script exists in the repo
npm run dev (without --turbopack) starts successfully; Next.js 16 uses Turbopack by default so the flag is redundant
Verified: curl POST /api/analyze returns full persona/pattern/comparison data (HTTP 200) using pre-cached demo data
16.1.assessment: A fresh clone CAN deploy and serve the demo flow following documented steps, because cache files are checked into src/data/cache/. However, the README does not mention that the cache files must exist or that seed-demo.ts (which is referenced but missing) generates them. The --turbopack flag is harmless but unnecessary in Next.js 16. The .env step (copy .env.example → .env) is documented but optional for demo mode.
gaps: Missing seed-demo.ts script referenced by cache.ts:10 error message
README does not explain that src/data/cache/*.json contains pre-built demo data required for the demo flow
The `--turbopack` flag in README is redundant (Next.js 16 defaults to Turbopack)

16.2.title: Secrets management — how secrets reach runtime
evidence: .env.example:1-6 defines OKX_API_KEY, OKX_SECRET_KEY, OKX_PASSPHRASE with placeholder values
.env (gitignored): contains real OKX API credentials (key, secret, passphrase) + OnchainOS CLI path note
.env.local (gitignored): contains VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN — a JWT auto-generated by `vercel link`/`vercel dev`, not user-managed
.gitignore:8-10 ignores .env, .env.local, .env*.local — secrets are properly excluded from version control
src/lib/onchainos.ts:1-14 shells out to `onchainos` CLI via execSync; the CLI reads OKX credentials from environment variables at runtime — no inline secret usage in source code
.vercel/project.json confirms project is linked to Vercel (projectId: prj_b3PS3eS5TammYL6H8dm6049e9yy0, orgId: team_WiDBceN6VoOQgdZ2jORoLLwN)
.deploy-state.json is gitignored (.gitignore:42) and does not exist locally — no production deployment state evidence available
No source file references process.env.OKX_* directly; the OnchainOS CLI binary reads env vars independently
16.2.assessment: Secrets management is adequate for the hackathon stage. Local dev: OKX keys in gitignored .env; Vercel OIDC token auto-injected by Vercel CLI. Production (Vercel): env vars would be configured via Vercel Dashboard → Project Settings → Environment Variables (standard Vercel pattern). The OnchainOS CLI decouples secrets from the Next.js app — the CLI binary reads env vars, not the TypeScript source. One concern: the .env.local VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN (a valid JWT) is committed to a transcript but not to the repo.
gaps: No evidence of Vercel Dashboard env var configuration (expected: OKX_API_KEY, OKX_SECRET_KEY, OKX_PASSPHRASE set in Vercel Project Settings)
No .deploy-state.json to confirm production deployment pipeline exists
No runtime env-var validation at startup — if OKX keys are missing, the live-mode code path fails only when an API call is made, not at boot

16.3.title: Startup order & health checks
evidence: package.json scripts: dev (next dev), build (next build), start (next start) — standard Next.js lifecycle
No database, Redis, or external service dependencies — package.json dependencies are: next, react, react-dom, framer-motion, tailwindcss, playwright (dev only), typescript (dev only)
npm run dev starts reliably: observed '✓ Ready in 376ms' and HTTP 200 on first request
npm run dev (without --turbopack) also starts with Turbopack — Next.js 16 uses Turbopack by default; flag is redundant
Turbopack root warning (multiple lockfiles at /Users/MAC/ and /Users/MAC/hackathon-toolkit/active/alter-ego/) is cosmetic only, does not block startup
No health check endpoint exists (no /api/health, no readiness probe)
No async service initialization — the app is a pure SSR Next.js app; no race conditions possible
16.3.assessment: Startup is reliable and fast (376ms). No service dependencies means no ordering issues or race conditions. The app is a pure Next.js SSR app. The turbopack root warning is a cosmetic issue in monorepo-like setups but does not affect functionality. Missing health check endpoint is acceptable for a hackathon demo but would be needed for production Kubernetes/container orchestration.
gaps: No /api/health or readiness endpoint for container orchestration
Cosmetic turbopack root warning in monorepo setup (can be silenced by setting turbopack.root in next.config.ts)

overall_assessment: DEPLOYABLE — The app deploys and runs reliably. A fresh clone can serve the demo flow without API keys because cache data is checked into the repo. Secrets are properly gitignored and managed through environment variables. The OnchainOS CLI decouples API credentials from the application source. No external service dependencies means zero startup ordering risks. Main gaps: (1) missing seed-demo.ts script referenced in error messages, (2) no evidence of Vercel production env var configuration, (3) no health check endpoint.
